name: Black Sesame Horchata With Ube and Coconut

ingredients.name: uncooked long-grain rice, rinsed until water runs clear
Mexican cinnamon stick, broken into large pieces
water, plus up to 4 cups for diluting

instructions.primary_message: In a large bowl, combine rice, black sesame seeds, shredded coconut, cinnamon, and 4 cups coconut water. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours and up to 24 hours.

Set a fine-mesh strainer over a large bowl and line it with a double layer of cheesecloth. Working in batches, if needed, transfer soaked mixture with soaking liquid to blender and blend on high until completely smooth, about 2 minutes. If mixture is too thick to blend, add additional coconut water, 1/4 cup at a time as needed to help blend. Pour mixture through prepared strainer, scraping bottom of strainer with spoon or rubber spatula to help liquid pass through. Discard solids.

Rinse blender. Return strained liquid to blender and add ube halaya and coconut cream. Blend until smooth, thick, and creamy, adding additional coconut water as needed to achieve desired consistency. Transfer to serving pitcher and serve in individual glasses over ice.

description: Learn how to make creamy black sesame horchata with ube, coconut, and rice for a rich, nutty twist on the classic Mexican drink.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 4 hr 10 min to 5 min.

Notes: Ube halaya is a sweet Filipino jam made from purple yam. It’s available at Filipino and many Asian grocery stores, as well as online.
Look for unsweetened canned coconut cream such as Savoy brand, which is thicker and richer than canned coconut milk. Do not substitute sweetened cream of coconut, which is intended for cocktails.
author: Octavio Peña
